_comment: Settings for `crewctl usage push`, which sends Kiro Crew's credit usage to an OTLP backend. Export is OFF while every endpoint is empty. Run `crewctl usage push --dry-run` to see exactly what would be sent.
_endpoint_comment: endpoint: the base URL of an OTLP/HTTP receiver (an OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana Alloy, grafana/otel-lgtm, Grafana Cloud). Logs go to <endpoint>/v1/logs and metrics to <endpoint>/v1/metrics. For VictoriaLogs and VictoriaMetrics, leave endpoint empty and set the two full URLs instead: http://HOST:9428/insert/opentelemetry/v1/logs and http://HOST:8428/opentelemetry/v1/metrics.
_auth_comment: headers_file: a file only you can read (chmod 600) with one 'Header-Name: value' per line, for example 'Authorization: Bearer ...'. It is refused if other users can read it, and over plain http to another machine unless allow_insecure_http is true.
_resource_comment: resource_attributes: a few labels for this machine, for example {"deployment.environment": "client-a", "service.instance.id": "laptop-1"}. service.name is kiro-crew unless you set it here.
_privacy_comment: drop_fields: never send these. Allowed: agent, workspace, app, session_key, session_id, parent_session_key, parent_session_id, subagent_id, stop_reason, context. hash_fields: send a keyed hash instead of the name (the key stays in the local state folder). Allowed: agent, workspace, app, session_key, session_id, parent_session_key, parent_session_id, subagent_id. Prompt and response text, file paths, cwd and error text are never sent.
_limits_comment: backfill_days: on the first run, usage files older than this are skipped (Loki refuses records older than 7 days by default). The other limits keep each run small.
